_comment: C0-14 d-id bodies EN. 无附加小节。正文「相关条目」4 行带 .md 链接（heygen/synthesia/runway/elevenlabs），related 写 4 条。sources 3 条对齐 frontmatter。

axes.model_access: Photo-driven digital-human line (Talking Photo: one photo + audio → talking-head video, the official signature narrative) + real-time interactive digital-human line (Agents, as seen in site navigation); the underlying models — no official statement verified item by item.
axes.runtime: Web (d-id.com) + API (an API entry on the official site; developer-facing is its traditional strength); generation on the vendor's cloud.
axes.local_files: Works stored account-side in the cloud, generation history visible on the web works page; downloads go local. No officially stated local data surface.
axes.background: Generation is instant/queued (varies by tier, not verified item by item); the real-time Agents line is streaming interaction (official narrative); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified).
axes.tools: Talking Photo (photo talking-head), real-time interactive digital humans (Agents line: customer-service/sales-guide scenario narratives), a video-translation line (seen on the official site); the API-first integration surface is its differentiating product posture.
axes.context: The Agents line has session state (an interactive digital human's conversation-memory surface exists; details not verified item by item); the creation side is organized by projects.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription + enterprise system (D9: prices not collected); **consent verification for real-photo-driven generation is the key compliance surface** (official consent narrative, details not verified line by line).
axes.fit: Fits: light batch photo→talking-head (historical figures/illustrated characters speaking), API-integrated digital humans, testing real-time interactive customer service. Does not fit: long-form video narrative, high-fidelity real-person cloning (HeyGen territory), cinematic-grade visual generation.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Talking Photo's quality falloff on non-frontal photos / stylized illustrations**
- **The real-time Agents line's latency and interruption behavior**
- **The capability gap between the API rendering queue and the web tiers**
unknowns:
- The underlying generation model (no official statement verified)
- Session-memory persistence on the Agents line (not verified item by item)
- The training-use switch (not verified line by line)
- Payment/account surfaces beyond mainland reachability (unverified)
related: Both digital humans: HeyGen leans on cloning/translation lines, D-ID is lighter on photo-driven/API orientation.
Both enterprise-oriented: Synthesia leans on the training workspace, D-ID on the integration surface.
Another species of video generation: Runway builds visuals, D-ID makes photos talk.
Upstream of the talking track: Talking Photo's audio is often supplied by ElevenLabs-style TTS; the two lines are commonly paired.
